001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
004import java.nio.CharBuffer;
005import java.nio.charset.Charset;
006import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
007import java.util.BitSet;
008
009/**
010 * Percent encoding (<a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986#section-2.1">RFC
011 * 3986</a>), the encoding Rainbow Gum uses for URI query properties and for key values
012 * written with
013 * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.KeyValuesFormatterBuilder.Format#PERCENT}, so that
014 * key values read from a log decode back to exactly what was logged.
015 */
016public final class PercentCodec {
017
018        private PercentCodec() {
019        }
020
021        static final BitSet GEN_DELIMS = new BitSet(256);
022        static final BitSet SUB_DELIMS = new BitSet(256);
023        static final BitSet UNRESERVED = new BitSet(256);
024        static final BitSet URIC = new BitSet(256);
025
026        static {
027                GEN_DELIMS.set(':');
028                GEN_DELIMS.set('/');
029                GEN_DELIMS.set('?');
030                GEN_DELIMS.set('#');
031                GEN_DELIMS.set('[');
032                GEN_DELIMS.set(']');
033                GEN_DELIMS.set('@');
034
035                SUB_DELIMS.set('!');
036                SUB_DELIMS.set('$');
037                SUB_DELIMS.set('&');
038                SUB_DELIMS.set('\'');
039                SUB_DELIMS.set('(');
040                SUB_DELIMS.set(')');
041                SUB_DELIMS.set('*');
042                SUB_DELIMS.set('+');
043                SUB_DELIMS.set(',');
044                SUB_DELIMS.set(';');
045                SUB_DELIMS.set('=');
046
047                for (int i = 'a'; i <= 'z'; i++) {
048                        UNRESERVED.set(i);
049                }
050                for (int i = 'A'; i <= 'Z'; i++) {
051                        UNRESERVED.set(i);
052                }
053                // numeric characters
054                for (int i = '0'; i <= '9'; i++) {
055                        UNRESERVED.set(i);
056                }
057                UNRESERVED.set('-');
058                UNRESERVED.set('.');
059                UNRESERVED.set('_');
060                UNRESERVED.set('~');
061                URIC.or(SUB_DELIMS);
062                URIC.or(UNRESERVED);
063        }
064
065        private static final int RADIX = 16;
066
067        static void encode(final StringBuilder buf, final CharSequence content, Charset charset, final BitSet safechars) {
068                final CharBuffer cb = CharBuffer.wrap(content);
069                final ByteBuffer bb = charset.encode(cb);
070                while (bb.hasRemaining()) {
071                        final int b = bb.get() & 0xff;
072                        if (safechars.get(b)) {
073                                buf.append((char) b);
074                        }
075                        else {
076                                buf.append("%");
077                                final char hex1 = Character.toUpperCase(Character.forDigit((b >> 4) & 0xF, RADIX));
078                                final char hex2 = Character.toUpperCase(Character.forDigit(b & 0xF, RADIX));
079                                buf.append(hex1);
080                                buf.append(hex2);
081                        }
082                }
083        }
084
085        /**
086         * Appends the content percent encoded: every byte of its encoding in the charset
087         * other than the unreserved characters <code>A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~</code> is written as
088         * <code>%XX</code> with upper case hex digits.
089         * @param buf output.
090         * @param content text to encode.
091         * @param charset charset of the bytes to encode, usually UTF-8.
092         */
093        public static void encode(final StringBuilder buf, final CharSequence content, final Charset charset) {
094                if (charset.equals(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
095                        encodeUtf8(buf, content);
096                }
097                else {
098                        encode(buf, content, charset, UNRESERVED);
099                }
100        }
101
102        /*
103         * UTF-8, the charset key values are always encoded with, straight from the chars: no
104         * CharBuffer view (whose per char charAt dispatch is what made CharBuffer.wrap slow
105         * in DirectByteBufferBuffer) and no ByteBuffer per call. A lone surrogate is written
106         * as ? (%3F), the same replacement Charset.encode uses, so the output is identical to
107         * the general path.
108         */
109        static void encodeUtf8(final StringBuilder buf, final CharSequence content) {
110                final int length = content.length();
111                for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
112                        char c = content.charAt(i);
113                        if (c < 0x80 && UNRESERVED_ASCII[c]) {
114                                // copy a run of unreserved characters at once, the common case for key
115                                // values
116                                final int start = i;
117                                while (i + 1 < length && (c = content.charAt(i + 1)) < 0x80 && UNRESERVED_ASCII[c]) {
118                                        i++;
119                                }
120                                buf.append(content, start, i + 1);
121                        }
122                        else if (c < 0x80) {
123                                appendByte(buf, c);
124                        }
125                        else if (c < 0x800) {
126                                appendByte(buf, 0xC0 | (c >> 6));
127                                appendByte(buf, 0x80 | (c & 0x3F));
128                        }
129                        else if (Character.isSurrogate(c)) {
130                                if (Character.isHighSurrogate(c) && i + 1 < length && Character.isLowSurrogate(content.charAt(i + 1))) {
131                                        final int cp = Character.toCodePoint(c, content.charAt(++i));
132                                        appendByte(buf, 0xF0 | (cp >> 18));
133                                        appendByte(buf, 0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3F));
134                                        appendByte(buf, 0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F));
135                                        appendByte(buf, 0x80 | (cp & 0x3F));
136                                }
137                                else {
138                                        appendByte(buf, '?');
139                                }
140                        }
141                        else {
142                                appendByte(buf, 0xE0 | (c >> 12));
143                                appendByte(buf, 0x80 | ((c >> 6) & 0x3F));
144                                appendByte(buf, 0x80 | (c & 0x3F));
145                        }
146                }
147        }
148
149        private static final char[] HEX = "0123456789ABCDEF".toCharArray();
150
151        private static final boolean[] UNRESERVED_ASCII = new boolean[0x80];
152
153        static {
154                for (int i = 0; i < 0x80; i++) {
155                        UNRESERVED_ASCII[i] = UNRESERVED.get(i);
156                }
157        }
158
159        private static void appendByte(final StringBuilder buf, final int b) {
160                buf.append('%').append(HEX[(b >> 4) & 0xF]).append(HEX[b & 0xF]);
161        }
162
163        /**
164         * Percent encodes the content, see
165         * {@link #encode(StringBuilder, CharSequence, Charset)}.
166         * @param content text to encode.
167         * @param charset charset of the bytes to encode, usually UTF-8.
168         * @return encoded text.
169         */
170        public static String encode(final CharSequence content, final Charset charset) {
171                final StringBuilder buf = new StringBuilder();
172                encode(buf, content, charset);
173                return buf.toString();
174        }
175
176        /**
177         * Decodes <code>%XX</code> sequences into bytes and the bytes into text with the
178         * charset. A <code>%</code> not followed by two hex digits is kept as is, and
179         * <code>+</code> is not a space. Characters that are not ASCII are kept as is, so
180         * text that was never encoded, such as a configured value, decodes to itself.
181         * @param content percent encoded text.
182         * @param charset charset of the encoded bytes, usually UTF-8.
183         * @return decoded text.
184         */
185        public static String decode(final CharSequence content, Charset charset) {
186                final ByteBuffer bb = ByteBuffer
187                        .allocate((int) Math.ceil(content.length() * (double) charset.newEncoder().maxBytesPerChar()));
188                final CharBuffer cb = CharBuffer.wrap(content);
189                while (cb.hasRemaining()) {
190                        final char c = cb.get();
191                        if (c >= 0x80) {
192                                // Keep a surrogate pair together so the charset encodes the code point.
193                                if (Character.isHighSurrogate(c) && cb.hasRemaining()
194                                                && Character.isLowSurrogate(cb.get(cb.position()))) {
195                                        bb.put(charset.encode(CharBuffer.wrap(new char[] { c, cb.get() })));
196                                }
197                                else {
198                                        bb.put(charset.encode(CharBuffer.wrap(new char[] { c })));
199                                }
200                        }
201                        else if (c == '%' && cb.remaining() >= 2) {
202                                final char uc = cb.get();
203                                final char lc = cb.get();
204                                final int u = Character.digit(uc, RADIX);
205                                final int l = Character.digit(lc, RADIX);
206                                if (u != -1 && l != -1) {
207                                        bb.put((byte) ((u << 4) + l));
208                                }
209                                else {
210                                        bb.put((byte) '%');
211                                        bb.put((byte) uc);
212                                        bb.put((byte) lc);
213                                }
214                        }
215                        else {
216                                bb.put((byte) c);
217                        }
218                }
219                bb.flip();
220                return charset.decode(bb).toString();
221        }
222
223}
